The '''1934–35 [[Primeira Liga|Campeonato da Liga]]''' season was the first season of top-tier [[Association football|football]] in [[Portugal]]. Although that, the most important national competition (in a knock-out cup format) was still called [[Taça de Portugal#1922–1938: Campeonato de Portugal|Portuguese Championship]], until 1938, the competition was considered not very competitive with a reduced number of matches played by each team. So a new competition, in round-robin format was created ind 1934, with 8 clubs. Although at time the winner of the Portuguese Championship was considered the National Champion, later, the winner of Campeonato da Liga 1934–35 would be considered the first National Champion.<ref>{{cite news|title=O FC Porto venceria o jogo após prolongamento (3x1), sagrando-se o primeiro campeão de Portugal.|url=https://www.zerozero.pt/text.php?id=11482/|access-date=24 February 2020|publisher=zerozero,pt|date=20 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Portuguese FA confirms Sporting has only 18 national titles|url=http://observador.pt/2016/12/16/federacao-confirma-sporting-tem-18-e-nao-22-titulos-de-campeao/|access-date=1 March 2017|publisher=observador,pt|date=16 December 2016}}</ref>

For the tournament, there were invited 8 clubs from the 4 major [[Portuguese District Football Associations]]: 4 teams from [[Lisbon Football Association|Lisbon FA]], 2 from [[Porto Football Association|Porto FA]], 1 from [[Setúbal Football Association|Setúbal FA]] and 1 from [[Coimbra Football Association|Coimbra FA]]. [[F.C. Porto]] won the championship. There were no relegations or promotions, since qualification was based on the results of the Regional Championships.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=9114 |title=Pesquisa – Jornal Record<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2015-01-21 |archive-date=2015-09-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924112123/http://www.record.xl.pt/Arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=9114 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
